_what: Calendars a space's members use together (src/space-calendars.mjs). Each member's own account shares only when they are busy (each stretch's start and end, never a title or anything else) with the spaces they are in, unless they turn it off for a space; find_space_times reads every member's busy stretches and answers the times everyone is free. A meeting put on in a space is placed on each member's own calendar through their own connection, once per meeting, and follows when it moves or they stop going. `calendars` are the kinds of calendar a member may have connected, tried in order: each names the connection a member connects (`service`, what connect_service takes), the calendar used (`calendar_id`), the shared Workshop tools that read busy times, create, move and cancel an event, and which account the connection is (`account`: a tool, its input with {now} filled in, and the path to the account's name in its reply; read only for the member asking about themself, so nobody's address reaches anyone else), where each reply keeps what is read (`reply`, read by src/space-calendars.mjs busyStretches). A new kind of calendar is one row here. `defaults` fill what find_space_times is not told; `limits` bound one search. `words` are everything said. `changed` is the message everyone in a space gets, from whoever did it, when a meeting moves or is cancelled ({title} filled in). `ask` is how Trillion asks a member whose calendar is not connected, never the person who searched: one thing in the space given to that member (its `facts`: `assignee` their shown name, `connects` the service, so Waiting on you closes it by itself once it is connected, src/waiting-on-you.json `done_when_connected`), placed by Trillion (origin trillion), with `link` the exact page that connects it; one per member and service across all their spaces, never a second while one is open.

words.everyone_free: These are times everyone in {space} is free.
words.some_unknown: These are times the {seen} of {total} people in {space} whose calendars Trillion can read are free. Not known for {unknown}.
words.nobody_known: Trillion cannot read anyone's calendar in {space} yet, so it cannot say when people are free.
words.no_times: Nobody whose calendar Trillion can read is free for {minutes} minutes together in that stretch.
words.not_connected_you: Automatic calendar availability is not connected. You can still reply with times and receive ordinary invitations.
words.not_connected_other: Automatic calendar availability is not connected for {name}. Their availability is unknown; they can still reply with times and receive ordinary invitations.
words.not_shared_you: You turned off using your calendar in this pursuit.
words.not_shared_other: {name} turned off using their calendar in this space.
words.unreadable: {name}'s calendar could not be read just now.
words.choice_on: Trillion now reads when you are busy for {space} and puts its meetings on your calendar.
words.choice_off: Trillion no longer reads your calendar for {space} or puts new meetings from it on your calendar.
words.too_many_members: This space has more than {most} people, so Trillion does not look through everyone's calendar at once.
words.bad_time: {field} is a time of day like 09:00.
words.bad_zone: time_zone is a place's time zone, like America/New_York.
words.bad_stretch: to comes after from, at most {days} days later.
words.bad_minutes: duration_minutes is a whole number from {shortest} to {longest}.
words.not_in_space: You are not a member of that pursuit.
words.bad_time: Give the time you are writing at, in milliseconds.

changed.moved: I moved "{title}" to a new time. It is on the Calendar.
changed.cancelled: I cancelled "{title}". It is off everyone's calendar.

ask.title: Connect your {service_name}
ask.text: {name}, connecting your {service_name} lets Trillion check availability automatically for {space}. To enable it, open the link, sign in and review the requested access. You can also reply with your available times; a connection is not required to receive or answer ordinary invitations. This step closes itself once the calendar is connected.
